clue.text: Die shaping advice to inveterate counterfeiter

definitions.meaning: a metalworking process that shapes hot metal by hammering it between dies
read as a phrase, it tells a habitual forger to give up the fakery

explanation.definitionFit: Hammering heated metal into a die is the industrial process named; split into two words it urges a forger to quit.

clue.text: Cross a small area of land

definitions.meaning: a crucifix, especially one above a church screen
an old English measure of land, a quarter of an acre

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crucifix in a church and an obsolete quarter-acre land measure.

clue.text: A rustic worker loaded with vegetables

indicators.note: in a down clue the worker carries the vegetables on top of it, so they come first

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A farm labourer weighed down with a crop of greens.
explanation.definitionFit: A countryman who works the land is a traditional rustic figure.

clue.text: Refuse the sorted sort

indicators.note: things sorted are put into a new order, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about which rubbish gets sorted from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps or leftovers of food are refuse.

clue.text: Decay in an entrance used by the strangler

indicators.note: the word for decay sits inside the word for an entrance

explanation.surface: A rotting gateway where a killer lurks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord or wire tightened round the neck is the killing tool of a strangler.

clue.text: Want Eden restored

indicators.note: restoring means rebuilding, so the letters of the garden are put back in another order

explanation.surface: A longing for paradise to be brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to require or lack it.

clue.text: Presumably they quickly became bosom pals

definitions.text: Presumably they quickly became bosom pals

parts.words: Presumably they quickly became bosom pals
parts.note: close companions are described with an adjective that also means speedy, so the clue pretends their friendship formed at speed

explanation.definitionFit: Firm, loyal companions are described this way; the adjective means firmly fixed, though it also means quick.

clue.text: A bloomer in funds built up for accommodating orders

indicators.note: the flower sits inside the word for funds

parts.note: an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: Someone has made a blunder with money set aside for building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but is a flower; 'orders' are religious communities, not commands.
explanation.definitionFit: These buildings house monks, members of religious orders.

clue.text: Mind reaches out for the goods

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A shopper reaching for products on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods for sale are a trader's wares.

clue.text: See me lose on being replaced? Not me!

indicators.note: letters being replaced are put back in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A loser hoping a replacement takes the blame instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting 'Not me!' points to another person instead of oneself.

clue.text: A little more may be added just for it to become effective legislation

definitions.text: A little more may be added just for it
definitions.meaning: an extra amount added as a bonus is added 'for' this phrase
a sound law or bill is a good one

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'for good measure' means as an extra; read literally, the words describe a sound legislative act.

clue.text: Not up to one of the garden plots

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener choosing between the flower plots.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still in bed has not yet got up.

clue.text: It is dead, dead, dead

parts.note: the repeated word stresses total, final extinction, as in the saying about the extinct flightless bird of Mauritius

explanation.definitionFit: This extinct bird gives the saying 'dead as a ...', meaning utterly lifeless.

clue.text: Tom upset the one that he may look at by constant change of course

indicators.note: upset tips the word over so it reads backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

parts.words: the one that he may look at
parts.note: the proverb says a cat may look at a king

explanation.surface: A sulky tomcat staring at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a cat may look at a king' means even a lowly person may look at a superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing into the wind, a boat zigzags by repeatedly turning across it.

clue.text: 1000 notes are played on it

definitions.meaning: slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a thousand pounds, and short for the large concert piano on which notes are played.

clue.text: Send around gratuity money for the pastor

indicators.note: the word send goes round the word for a gratuity

explanation.surface: A collection is passed round for the minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's fixed salary is traditionally called this.

clue.text: In the home counties private transport creates panic

indicators.note: the vehicle goes inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: SE, the South East, the region round London known in Britain as the home counties

explanation.surface: Commuter car traffic around London causing alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the English counties around London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden fright is a panic.

clue.text: Broken cruet leads to cessation of hostilities

indicators.note: the cruet is smashed so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smashed table condiment set starts a ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreed halt to fighting is an armistice.

clue.text: Bring up what those who come last bring up

definitions.text: what those who come last bring up
definitions.meaning: those at the back 'bring up the' back part

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to raise a child; the noun is the back position in the phrase 'bring up the ...'.

clue.text: Formerly one per cent-or just the opposite

indicators.note: per means through, so one word is passed through the other
reverses the order of the container, so the cent goes through the word one

explanation.surface: A remark about percentages and their reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One per cent' would put ONE through C; 'just the opposite' swaps them, so C goes inside ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: At one time in the past means formerly.

clue.text: Poles are all for gin

parts.note: S and N, the south and north poles

explanation.surface: People from Poland are all in favour of a glass of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a trap for animals, as is a noose or net.

clue.text: Did he win seat Ron reserved for him last autumn?

definitions.text: Did he win seat Ron reserved for him last autumn?

indicators.note: reserved read as re-served, the letters dealt out again in a new order

explanation.surface: An election question about whether a man named Ron took the seat saved for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who wins a seat in an upper house, as in an autumn US election.

clue.text: Give authority to overthrow Middle Eastern state

indicators.note: overthrown in a down clue, the abbreviation is turned upside down

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for Middle East
a power is a state or nation

explanation.surface: A call for a revolution against a Middle Eastern regime.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise someone is to grant them power.

clue.text: Tolerated nude pose, but finally embarrassed

indicators.note: the word for embarrassed is put at the end
pose means to arrange or position, so the four letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Someone put up with posing naked, only to blush at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pose' looks like the nude model's stance but is the anagram signal; 'embarrassed' gives a blushing colour, and 'but finally' puts it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Endured means put up with or bore patiently.

clue.text: Ruler showing a printer's measure used by a printing machine

parts.note: an em is a unit of measure in printing

explanation.surface: A monarch shown in a printing shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sovereign of an empire is a ruler.

clue.text: Is in current use as a computer filing system

indicators.note: the little word goes inside the abbreviation for current

explanation.surface: A claim about which computer storage is in common use now.
explanation.definitionFit: A disk stores files on a computer.

clue.text: Austere Roman hi-tech establishment comes to nought

indicators.note: the zero comes after the college, below it in a down clue

parts.note: CAT is a College of Advanced Technology, a British technical college

explanation.surface: A high-tech company comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: CAT stood for College of Advanced Technology, a kind of British technical college of the 1950s and 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman famed for strict, severe morals.

clue.text: Part of speech found in clever book

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the run of these two words

explanation.surface: Learning grammar from a clever book.
explanation.definitionFit: A doing word is one of the parts of speech.

clue.text: Holy man upset a king-a Russian one

indicators.note: upset turns the abbreviation backwards

parts.note: R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A saint upsets a monarch from Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia's former emperors were called by this title, so one was a Russian king.

clue.text: Run as a moderate or an extreme leftist

definitions.meaning: to run at a moderate pace
a Trotskyist, a far-left supporter of Trotsky

explanation.definitionFit: A gentle running pace, and short for a Trotskyist on the far left.

clue.text: Production of it involves rare new heat

definitions.text: Production of it involves rare new heat

indicators.note: the letters are produced in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Making pottery needs fresh, intense firing in the kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: Fired clay pottery is made in a hot kiln.

clue.text: Back up because Corinthians steal and blab

parts.note: COR is the abbreviation for the Bible book of Corinthians
to orate is to speak at length

explanation.surface: Confirming that a football team's players thieve and gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm or support a claim with evidence is to back it up.
